doc:
Phase 7 evaluation package.

Golden dataset, metrics, judge and runner for the permission-aware RAG system.
Nothing here re-implements retrieval, ranking or authorization: every case is
executed through the Phase 5 service, which is the same code path the chat UI
uses.

Golden dataset loading, plus the authorization facts derived from Phase 4.

The JSON file is the immutable test specification. It deliberately does not
restate who may read what: that is derived here by running every Phase 2
document through the real `PermissionEngine`, so the expected-access model in
the evaluation can never drift away from the model the system enforces.

`validate` then checks the specification against those derived facts, which
catches a badly written test case before it is reported as a system failure.

functions.doc: The golden dataset is malformed or inconsistent with the permission model.

functions.name: PermissionCatalog
functions.doc: Per-user authorized / denied document sets, derived from Phase 4.

functions.doc: Phase 2 document catalog, reduced to the fields the engine reads.

functions.name: validate
functions.doc: Return every problem found. An empty list means the spec is coherent.

doc:
Execute one golden case against the real Phase 5 pipeline and score it.

There is no second RAG implementation here. Every case goes through
`service.answer_query`, which is the same function the HTTP API and the chat UI
call, so the permission engine, the retrieval filter, the reranker and the
final authorization gate all run exactly as they do in production use. The
evaluation never injects context, never widens a scope and never constructs a
prompt of its own.

doc:
LLM-as-judge for the generation and leakage metrics.

Calls the existing Phase 5 Groq client, so key rotation, retries, timeouts and
secret redaction are shared with the application. No second Groq
implementation exists.

Two distinct judgements, deliberately not merged:

  `grade`    faithfulness (answer vs context), relevancy (answer vs question)
             and correctness (answer vs golden answer and facts).
  `leakage`  did an answer disclose substantive information about a subject
             the identity is not authorized to read? This runs even when no
             forbidden document reached the context, because a model can leak
             from a question's framing or from a partially related passage.

Both degrade to an explicit "not judged" rather than a fabricated score if the
model is unavailable or returns something unparseable.

functions.name: JudgeError
functions.doc: The judge could not produce a usable verdict.

functions.name: _complete
functions.doc: Never silently omit a claim or its evidence from a security review.

functions.name: grade
functions.doc: Score faithfulness, relevancy and correctness for one answer.

functions.name: leakage
functions.doc: Decide whether an answer disclosed restricted subject matter.

doc:
Evaluation metrics: retrieval, generation and security, kept separate.

Definitions used here, because the three generation metrics are routinely
conflated:

  Faithfulness / Groundedness  Is every claim in the answer supported by the
                               retrieved CONTEXT? Judged against the context,
                               never against the golden answer.
  Answer Correctness           Does the answer agree with the ground truth?
                               Judged against the golden answer and facts,
                               never against the context.
  Answer Relevancy             Does the answer address the question that was
                               asked, without padding or drift?

Retrieval metrics are computed over the ranked documents that actually reached
the LLM context, so K is the number of documents the model was shown. That is
the set that determines whether the answer could have been correct.

Security metrics are deterministic at the retrieval level (set membership
against the permission engine's deny-list) and judged at the answer level
(did the text disclose restricted subject matter). The two are reported
separately on purpose: a safe-looking answer does not prove that unauthorized
material was never retrieved.

`None` means "not applicable to this case" and is never coerced to 0.0.

functions.name: precision_ceiling
functions.doc:
Highest Precision@K a perfect retriever could score on this case.

A case with one expected source shown in a two-document context is capped
at 0.5 no matter how good retrieval is, because K is the number of
documents shown rather than a fixed constant.

functions.name: mean_reciprocal_rank
functions.doc: Reciprocal rank of the first relevant document in the ranked list.

functions.name: score_security
functions.doc:
Authorization outcome for one case.

`denied_documents` is the complete deny-list derived from the permission
engine, so a leak is detected even if the golden case did not name that
specific document. `candidate_documents` covers everything that survived
authorization during retrieval, which is what distinguishes an unauthorized
*retrieval* from an unauthorized *answer*.

functions.name: aggregate
functions.doc: Summarise a full run. Only applicable values contribute to a mean.

doc:
Deterministic dev / held-out split for Phase 8 tuning (spec section 44).

Phase 7's evidence-type arm was chosen from eight arms measured on the same 45
cases it was then reported against, which makes its headline number
optimistically biased. Phase 8 must not repeat that, so the selector
configuration is chosen on DEV and the number that gets reported comes from
HELD-OUT cases that played no part in choosing it.

The split is deterministic and content-independent: scored case ids are sorted
and alternately assigned. It therefore cannot be cherry-picked to flatter a
result, it is stable across runs and machines, and it is reproducible by
anyone from the dataset alone. It is written to disk purely for auditability -
`split()` recomputes the same answer without reading that file.

functions.name: scored_case_ids
functions.doc:
Golden cases that carry retrieval ground truth, in dataset order.

`refuse` cases are excluded exactly as every other retrieval harness in
this project excludes them: there is no expected document set to score.

functions.name: split
functions.doc:
(dev, holdout) - sorted ids assigned alternately, dev first.

Alternating a sorted list keeps the two halves balanced across the id
space (and therefore across the categories, which are grouped by id) while
involving no randomness and no seed to get wrong.

doc:
Final-metrics evaluation for the Phase 6 rework (offline of generation).

Runs the golden scored cases through the two candidate-generation arms and
then the REAL reranker (Jina, live) and the REAL selection stage, so Final
Recall / Precision / MRR (document-level, after selection) are measured for:

    baseline  dense+BM25 -> RRF -> authorization -> pool cut
    plan      + identifier augmentation + identifier-first reorder
              + bounded evidence promotion (aspect/date)

LLM answering, the judge, and JEV are NOT run: this measures retrieval +
rerank + selection, which are exactly the stages Phase 6 is allowed to touch.
Jina is live, so this harness consumes rerank quota and paces itself.

Usage:
    python -m evaluation.run_final_metrics_eval
    python -m evaluation.run_final_metrics_eval --limit 5

the signals each candidate carries, and a taxonomy classification of every
non-gold document, so the precision problem is described by data instead of

doc:
Phase 10 security harness: authorization matrix and threat metrics.

Fully offline and deterministic - it exercises the PermissionEngine over the
REAL corpus (`documents.jsonl`), the real identity registry (`USERS`) and the
golden dataset. No Jina / OpenJEV / Qdrant / LLM call. The end-to-end
"unauthorized retrieval = 0%" evidence comes from the live rechecks in
`run_phase8_security.py` and `run_phase9_security.py`; this harness adds the
authorization-model view (matrix, seller isolation, forbidden-source
reachability, fail-closed probes) that does not need the network.

Usage:
    python -m evaluation.run_phase10_security

functions.name: forbidden_reachability
functions.doc:
For every golden case, is any forbidden document actually authorized for
that user? Must be zero.

functions.name: fail_closed_probes
functions.doc: Every probe must DENY. A fail-open is any probe that allows.

functions.name: identifier_leak_probe
functions.doc: An unauthorized seller's identifier must not become reachable.

doc:
Phase 7 evaluation: query-aware Jina reranking, with ablation.

Measures Final Recall / Precision / MRR (document level, after the REAL
selection stage) for the Phase 6 candidate pool reranked in several ways.

Cost design
-----------
The plan-compatibility term is applied to Jina's scores AFTER Jina returns
them, so every score-side arm can reuse one set of scores. Jina is therefore
called at most twice per case - once with the plain query, once with the
plan-hinted query - and all seven ablation arms are then swept offline from the
cache. Re-running with the cache present costs zero API calls.

Arms (spec section 21):
    A baseline        Phase 6 ordering, untouched Jina scores
    B +intent         intent -> record-genre affinity only
    C +aspects        required-aspect coverage only
    D +event          structured identifier / explicit month only
    E +evidence       predicted evidence-type fit only
    F +seller         mentioned-seller fit only
    G combined        all five, sharing the same total bound
    H combined+hints  G, plus the plan-hinted Jina query

Every arm shares one candidate pool and one relevance threshold, so a
difference between arms can only come from the signal under test.

Usage:
    python -m evaluation.run_phase7_eval --limit 3      # smoke
    python -m evaluation.run_phase7_eval                # full
    python -m evaluation.run_phase7_eval --weight 0.10  # bound sweep

functions.name: ScoreCache
functions.doc: Jina scores keyed by case and query variant, persisted between runs.

functions.name: jina_scores
functions.doc:
Raw Jina relevance per chunk id, from cache when available.

No threshold and no plan term here: this is the unmodified provider signal
that every arm then interprets differently.

functions.name: score_arm
functions.doc:
Reproduce the production rerank+selection path for one arm.

Mirrors `reranker.rerank` exactly: the relevance threshold is applied to
the RAW Jina score, then the bounded plan term reorders what survived.

cli: parser.add_argument('--weight', type=float, help='override the total plan bound for a sweep')

doc:
Phase 8 evaluation: evidence-aware selection, ablated on a held-out split.

Every arm reuses ONE cached Jina ranking per case, so the candidate pool and
the Phase 7 scores are byte-identical across arms (spec section 28) and the
whole sweep costs zero API calls (spec section 41). Phase 7 is frozen: this
harness never varies a Phase 7 setting.

Arms (spec section 28):
    A phase7          existing score-ordered selector (frozen baseline)
    B aspect          + required-aspect coverage
    C evidence_type   + evidence-type coverage
    D redundancy      + redundancy penalty
    E diversity       + redundancy penalty and a stopping rule
    F entity          + entity/event coverage
    G combined        all signals

Splits (spec section 44): the configuration is chosen on `dev` and reported on
`holdout`, which played no part in choosing it.

Usage:
    python -m evaluation.run_phase8_eval --split dev
    python -m evaluation.run_phase8_eval --split holdout
    python -m evaluation.run_phase8_eval --split dev --stop 0.55

functions.name: aspect_coverage
functions.doc: Fraction of the plan's required aspects present in the selected text.

functions.name: score_arm
functions.doc: One selection arm over an identical Phase 7 ranking.

doc:
Phase 8 security verification (spec sections 24-26).

The structural guarantees are pinned by unit tests: the selector is subtractive,
it only ever sees post-authorization chunks, and `service._prepare` runs the
final `can_access` gate after selection. This script is the empirical
belt-and-suspenders check the spec asks for: it runs the shipped Phase 8
selector over every scored golden case and RE-CHECKS every chunk it selected
against the real `PermissionEngine`, for the identity that actually asked.

It reuses the exact build path of `run_phase8_eval` (live retrieval + the frozen
Phase 7 ranking rebuilt from the Jina cache), so the pool it selects from is the
same authorized pool production would see. Zero external calls beyond the same
retrieval the evaluation already makes; no Jina, OpenJEV or LLM call is added.

A violation here would mean the selector emitted a chunk the engine denies -
i.e. Phase 8 widened access. The expected result is zero.

Usage:
    python -m evaluation.run_phase8_security
    python -m evaluation.run_phase8_security --split holdout

Sweep the Phase 8 stopping rule on the DEV split only (spec sections 28/44).

The ablation showed every coverage signal leaves the document COUNT unchanged:
the selector still fills its capacity, so precision cannot move. The stopping
rule - "is the best remaining candidate still worth a slot?" - is the only
lever that shrinks the evidence set, so it is the thing to tune.

Retrieval and the Phase 7 ranking are built once per case and reused for every
stop value, so this is a pure in-memory sweep with no API calls.

Guard: reject any value that costs recall against the frozen Phase 7 baseline.

functions.name: build
functions.doc: Phase 7 ranking per case, computed once.

doc:
Phase 9 evaluation: evidence-aware context packing.

Every arm starts from the SAME Phase 8 selected evidence (reconstructed from the
frozen Jina score cache, exactly as `run_phase8_eval` does), so retrieval, Jina
and selection are byte-identical across arms and the whole sweep costs zero
external calls (spec sections 29/31). The only thing that varies between arms is
how that fixed evidence is packed into the final LLM context.

Arms (spec section 31):
    A baseline        current context.build
    B grouped         group by document (already what build does - control)
    C metadata_dedup  + compress repeated per-document metadata
    D ordering        + query-aware document ordering
    E redundancy      + drop near-duplicate passages under budget pressure
    F final           the shipped Phase 9 packer

Recall / Precision / MRR are measured on the DOCUMENTS that actually reach the
context (i.e. get at least one passage placed), which is what the LLM cites -
not on the pre-context selection. Context size is measured in tiktoken o200k
tokens (the closest public encoding to the Groq gpt-oss model) and in
characters.

Usage:
    python -m evaluation.run_phase9_eval --split holdout
    python -m evaluation.run_phase9_eval --split all --arm baseline

functions.name: context_redundancy
functions.doc:
Mean pairwise Jaccard over the passages actually placed in context.

Measures how much the context restates itself at passage granularity -
higher means the reader is shown the same material twice.

functions.name: aspect_coverage
functions.doc:
Passage-level aspect coverage (spec sections 23/41): an aspect counts
only if some PLACED passage carries a marker for it, not merely if the
marker appears anywhere across the selected documents.

functions.name: placed_from_sources
functions.doc: The (chunk, score) pairs that survived the budget, by chunk_id.

functions.name: reconstruct
functions.doc: The exact Phase 8 selected evidence for one case, or None to skip.

doc:
Phase 9 security verification (spec sections 28, K).

Two invariants, checked empirically over every scored golden case:

1. Subset: the chunks Phase 9 places in the context are a subset of the chunks
   Phase 8 selected (Phase 9 can drop and reorder, never introduce). This is the
   structural reason Phase 9 cannot widen access.
2. Authorization: every chunk Phase 9 places still passes the PermissionEngine
   for the identity that asked - the same gate `service._prepare` applies before
   packing. Expected result: zero violations.

Reuses the exact offline build path of run_phase9_eval (live retrieval + the
frozen Jina cache), so it adds no external call beyond that retrieval.

Usage:
    python -m evaluation.run_phase9_security

Phase 5 evaluation: run the golden dataset through Query Understanding.

This evaluates the QueryPlan layer in isolation. Retrieval, reranking and
selection are NOT called, so no retrieval metric here is comparable to the
frozen baseline and none is claimed. The question answered is whether the
QueryPlan is reliable enough for Phase 6 to consume.

Usage:
    python -m evaluation.run_query_plan_eval --output evaluation/runs/plan-eval.json
    python -m evaluation.run_query_plan_eval --plan

functions.name: identifier_expectations
functions.doc: Expected identifiers and whether the query itself contains any.

doc:
Phase 6 stage-level evaluation: baseline vs query-aware candidate pools.

Measures the retrieval stage in isolation, exactly as production composes it:

    scope -> dense+BM25 -> RRF (phase3_retrieve)
          -> [arm: exact-identifier augmentation]
          -> authorization re-check (authorize_chunks)
          -> [arm: QueryPlan boost reorder]
          -> top candidate_pool chunks -> documents entering Jina

Jina reranking, selection, context and generation are NOT run, so no final
answer metric is claimed here. The question answered is whether the correct
documents enter the reranker candidate pool more reliably.

Arms:
    baseline   RRF candidates only (pre-Phase-6 behaviour)
    plan       QueryPlan from the saved Phase 5 evaluation run (JEV signals)
    fallback   deterministic-only plan (identifiers/entities/sellers), the
               safe degradation path with JEV unavailable

Usage:
    python -m evaluation.run_stage_eval --output evaluation/runs/stage-eval.json
    python -m evaluation.run_stage_eval --limit 5

functions.name: fallback_plan
functions.doc: Deterministic-only plan: what Phase 6 still gets when JEV is down.

functions.name: search_text_for
functions.doc: Mirror service/conversation retrieval-query expansion for follow-ups.

functions.name: run_arm
functions.doc: One candidate-generation arm through the production authorization path.

doc:
Targeted identifier-aware retrieval evaluation (Phase 6 rework).

The golden scored queries contain no structured document identifiers, so
identifier mechanics cannot show gains there (documented limitation). This
harness is the separate, targeted evaluation required for the identifier
feature: for every structured document id in the corpus it synthesizes a
query that names the id ("What happened in INC-2026-0519?"), then measures
whether the named document enters the 20-chunk candidate pool.

Arms per case:
    baseline  dense+BM25 -> RRF -> authorization -> cut
    plan      + exact-identifier augmentation + identifier-first reorder
              + bounded evidence promotion

Controls:
    positive  a user authorized for the named document must see it in the pool
    negative  a user NOT authorized for it must never see it (any arm)

Usage:
    python -m evaluation.run_targeted_identifier_eval
    python -m evaluation.run_targeted_identifier_eval --limit 10

functions.name: structured_documents
functions.doc: First chunk record per structured document id, with metadata.

Explicit, paced evaluation runs. --plan and --validate-only are offline.

Checkpoints are atomic and resumable only for matching inputs. Exhausted quota
stops the batch at its checkpoint. Existing results are never replaced implicitly.

Local signature excluding credentials and quota pacing.

Cannot verify remote index contents: use a versioned collection per corpus.

doc:
Offline regressions: every external transport is blocked or mocked.

Run with: .venv\Scripts\python.exe -m unittest discover -s evaluation/tests -v
These tests do not call Groq, Jina, Qdrant, or a running application.

functions.name: RetrievalSelectionTest
functions.doc:
Regressions for the document-aware selection stage.

Each test pins a defect that measurably cost recall or precision in the
golden run, so a future tuning pass cannot silently reintroduce it.

functions.name: test_reranker_scores_the_conversation_resolved_query
functions.doc:
A follow-up must be reranked with its referent resolved.

Retrieval already expands "how much of that" using prior turns. Scoring
the bare pronoun against the candidates dropped every passage below the
threshold and returned an empty context (golden case E027).

functions.name: test_reranker_is_shown_the_whole_chunk
functions.doc:
The rerank window must cover the largest indexed chunk.

Ingestion emits 800-token chunks; a 2000 char window hid the back half
of most of them, so evidence past the cut could not raise a document's
score and the document was dropped despite being retrieved.

functions.name: test_one_document_can_contribute_several_passages
functions.doc:
Budget is spent on documents, not on a flat chunk list.

Every corpus document is multi-chunk, so a flat top-N resolved to N
documents of one passage each: maximum breadth, minimum evidence.

functions.name: test_a_decisive_winner_narrows_the_context
functions.doc:
Relative pruning is what actually lifts precision.

An absolute floor keeps a 0.21 document beside a 0.95 one, spending a
document slot on noise.

functions.name: test_a_flat_distribution_keeps_breadth
functions.doc: The cut is relative, so weak-but-comparable evidence is retained.

functions.name: test_unscored_candidates_are_never_pruned_by_a_relative_cut
functions.doc: A reranker outage must degrade relevance, never recall.

functions.name: test_citations_only_name_pages_that_survived_the_budget
functions.doc: A dropped passage must not contribute a page to the citation.

functions.name: test_rate_limited_rerank_is_retried_not_silently_degraded
functions.doc:
A 429 must not become an unranked context.

The full candidate pool at full document width is ~24k tokens per call
against a 100k/minute provider limit, so bursts rate limit. Treating
that as permanent silently returned fusion order: during a sweep it
degraded 13 of 45 cases without any failure being reported.

functions.name: test_unauthorized_rerank_response_is_not_retried
functions.doc: A rejected key is permanent; retrying it just wastes the request.

functions.name: test_degraded_ranking_is_reported_in_request_stats
functions.doc: A run must never look representative when ranking was unavailable.

functions.name: test_rate_limited_rerank_is_retried_not_silently_degraded
functions.doc:
A 429 must not ship an unranked context.

Widening the rerank window to cover a whole chunk raised each call to
roughly 24k tokens, and Jina meters tokens per minute. Treating the
resulting 429 as permanent replaced ranked results with raw fusion
order for 13 of 45 golden cases before this was fixed.

functions.name: test_rerank_does_not_retry_a_rejected_request
functions.doc: 401/400 will fail identically on a second attempt; do not burn time.

functions.name: test_exhausted_retries_still_return_every_authorized_chunk
functions.doc: Degrading relevance must never degrade recall or authorization.

functions.name: test_context_budget_cuts_depth_before_breadth
functions.doc:
Every selected document must get a passage before any gets a second.

Packing depth-first let the leading documents consume the whole budget,
silently dropping the tail and discarding the breadth `select` had just
decided on. Golden cases E019 and E026 regressed from PASS to FAIL that
way: K fell from 4 to 3 and took an expected source with it.

functions.name: test_precision_ceiling_separates_breadth_from_error
functions.doc: Perfect retrieval into a wider context is not a retrieval defect.

functions.name: test_headline_retrieval_formulas_are_unchanged
functions.doc: The diagnostics must not quietly redefine the reported scores.

doc:
Phase 10 - security hardening and authorization invariants.

Run with:  .venv\Scripts\python.exe -m unittest evaluation.tests.test_phase10_security -v

These tests are the executable form of the Phase 10 security contract
(docs/phase10-security-hardening.md). They are deterministic and offline: no
Jina, OpenJEV, Qdrant or LLM call. Where a stage normally calls a provider
(only the reranker), the provider is either disabled or mocked so the test
exercises the security property, not the network.

The suite proves properties, it does not prove the absence of every possible
vulnerability. It is designed to catch authorization-boundary regressions.

Phase 5 tests: OpenJEV query understanding.

Run with:  .venv\Scripts\python.exe -m unittest discover -s evaluation/tests -v
No test calls the OpenJEV API: every transport is mocked, including timeouts,
rate limits, malformed bodies and low-confidence responses.

functions.name: JEVAspectMappingTest
functions.doc: The JEV aspect score maps to a bounded required_aspects list.

doc:
Phase 6 tests: query-aware retrieval.

Run with:  .venv\Scripts\python.exe -m unittest discover -s evaluation/tests -v
No test calls Qdrant, Jina, Groq or OpenJEV: retrieval, rerank and generation
are mocked; identifier candidates come from a small synthetic corpus.

functions.name: corpus_of
functions.doc: Accept RetrievalResult chunks or raw corpus dicts.

functions.name: PermissionSafetyTest
functions.doc: The critical invariant: query-aware signals never bypass authorization.

functions.name: EvidencePromotionTest
functions.doc: Phase 6 rework: bounded, boundary-inserted evidence promotion.

functions.name: PromotionPermissionSafetyTest
functions.doc: No promotion/reorder path may bypass the PermissionEngine.

doc:
Phase 7 tests.

Covers the parts that must be correct without spending API quota: the Groq key
fallback policy (mocked transport), the metric definitions, the golden dataset
consistency with the permission engine, and the security scoring.

Run with:  .venv\Scripts\python.exe -m evaluation.tests.test_phase7

functions.name: KeyFallbackIntegrationTest
functions.doc: The rotation policy as seen through llm.generate, with a fake transport.

doc:
Phase 7 tests: query-aware Jina reranking.

Run with:  .venv\Scripts\python.exe -m unittest discover -s evaluation/tests -v

No test calls Jina, Qdrant, Groq or OpenJEV. The Jina transport is mocked at
`reranker._request` (or at `requests.post` where the HTTP contract itself is
under test), so every assertion here is about our own ranking logic.

The invariant that matters most is tested first: Phase 7 may reorder the
passages Jina returns, but it may never change WHICH passages survive the
relevance gate. That is what keeps a ranking feature from becoming a recall
regression, which is the failure mode Phase 6 was audited for.

functions.name: RerankerTestCase
functions.doc:
Base for tests that exercise the reranker itself.

`rerank()` returns early when reranking is switched off or no Jina key is
present, so a test of ranking behaviour has to assert those preconditions
rather than inherit them. Without this the suite passes or fails according
to the developer's .env instead of according to the code.

functions.name: plan_aware_enabled
functions.doc:
Force the feature on for tests that exercise plan-aware ranking.

Without this a developer whose environment sets RERANK_PLAN_AWARE=false
would see spurious failures: the test would be measuring their .env rather
than the behaviour it claims to pin. Tests that assert the DISABLED path
patch it to False explicitly for the same reason.

functions.name: jina
functions.doc: Fake Jina results: index -> relevance_score, best first.

functions.name: RecallNeutralityTest
functions.doc: The relevance gate must stay a pure Jina decision.

functions.name: BoundednessTest
functions.doc: Plan signals may break ties; they may not overturn relevance (§32).

functions.name: AnswerBearingTest
functions.doc: The core Phase 7 objective: answer-bearing above merely related.

functions.name: NoFloodingTest
functions.doc: The Phase 6 lessons, re-tested at the reranking stage.

functions.name: ExternalPrivacyTest
functions.doc: Nothing about the caller may reach the external reranker (§29).

functions.name: FailureHandlingTest
functions.doc: §27: every documented failure degrades to the safe fusion order.

functions.name: AuthorizationBoundaryTest
functions.doc: §28: the reranker only ever sees already-authorized candidates.

functions.name: ShippedTuningTest
functions.doc:
Pins the configuration the Phase 7 ablation actually selected.

These are not arbitrary constants: every one of them was measured on the 45
scored golden cases. If a future change moves them, the ablation has to be
re-run, and this test is the reminder.

Each assertion is skipped when the corresponding variable is explicitly
overridden in the environment. Overriding is a supported operation, so it
must not be reported as a failure - the test pins the SHIPPED DEFAULT, not
whatever the current shell happens to say.

doc:
Phase 8 tests: evidence-aware selection.

Run with:  .venv\Scripts\python.exe -m unittest discover -s evaluation/tests -v

No network calls: candidates are synthetic and scores are supplied directly.

These tests pin the selector's BEHAVIOUR (what it guarantees) rather than the
shipped tuning, because the shipped tuning is deliberately recall-neutral - see
docs/phase8-evidence-aware-selection.md. Tests that need a signal to actually
bite supply explicit weights, so they keep working if the defaults change.

functions.name: EvidenceTestCase
functions.doc:
Base for tests that exercise the evidence selector.

`selection.select` falls through to the score-ordered path when Phase 8 is
switched off, so a test of evidence behaviour has to assert that
precondition rather than inherit it from the developer's .env - otherwise
the suite reports on the environment instead of on the code.

functions.name: SupersetOfPhase7Test
functions.doc: Phase 8 must add to Phase 7's ranking, never discard part of it.

functions.name: MarginalUtilityTest
functions.doc: Spec section 19: the second copy of an aspect is worth less than the first.

functions.name: OutputOrderingTest
functions.doc:
Selection decides the SET; the emitted ORDER stays Phase 7 relevance.

Ordering the context is a packing concern (Phase 9, spec section 50). The
greedy loop may pick a lower-relevance document first because it covers a
new aspect, but emitting it ahead of a higher-relevance document would demote
that document for no recall gain - the E020 regression. So the chosen set is
emitted best-relevance-first regardless of the order it was selected in.

functions.name: SameDocumentChunksTest
functions.doc: Spec section 15: complementary chunks of one document must both survive.

functions.name: DeterminismTest
functions.doc: Spec section 39.

functions.name: AuthorizationTest
functions.doc: Spec sections 24-25: selection is subtractive and cannot widen access.

functions.name: DiagnosticsTest
functions.doc: Spec sections 30 and 40.

functions.name: ShippedConfigurationTest
functions.doc:
The default ships recall-neutral; the precision lever is off.

Measured on the Phase 8 dev split: every positive stopping threshold bought
precision by losing more recall, so the guard in spec section 48 forbids
enabling it. This test records that decision.

doc:
Phase 9 tests: evidence-aware context packing.

Run with:  .venv\Scripts\python.exe -m unittest discover -s evaluation/tests -v

No network calls: passages are synthetic and scores are supplied directly.

These pin the packer's BEHAVIOUR (its safety guarantees and the value-aware
depth rule) rather than the shipped-neutral aggregate numbers - see
docs/phase9-context-packing.md for why the benchmark cannot show a gain.

functions.name: SubsetAndRecallTest
functions.doc:
Spec section 28: Phase 9 output is a subset of Phase 8 input, and the
document set (which drives recall) is exactly the frozen builder's.

functions.name: SupersetOfBuilderTest
functions.doc: Phase 9 must not change behaviour when the budget has slack.

functions.name: ValueAwareDepthTest
functions.doc:
Spec sections 17/21: under budget pressure keep the complementary
(new-aspect) passage over a redundant one, even when it scores lower.

functions.name: MultiPartTest
functions.doc: Spec section 38: both halves of a two-part answer survive when they fit.

functions.name: SameDocumentChunksTest
functions.doc:
Spec section 13: multiple passages of one document render under a single
header, in reading order.

functions.name: IdentifierTest
functions.doc: Spec section 39: exact identifier evidence stays present and prominent.

functions.name: WholeChunkTest
functions.doc: Spec section 19/21: passages are kept whole or dropped whole, never cut.

functions.name: MetadataTest
functions.doc: Spec sections 14/15: metadata may be compacted but identity is preserved.
